ut_small_adventures_wall_313_slabs.blurb: A short roadside slab beside Highway 313 outside Moab, this sandstone wall is mostly bolted face and friction climbing on sticky, fairly featureless rock, with the odd edge, dish or huecos to pull on. Of its 17 climbs, 16 are sport routes and one is a boulder problem. Difficulty runs from easy fifth class up to the low 5.12s, but the bulk of the lines sit between 5.8 and 5.10, which makes it a handy pick for moderate leaders. Some routes can be top-roped from a ledge on the left side. Watch for loose flakes and plates in places. It is a quick, low-commitment stop rather than a full-day destination.

ut_zion_s_crag.blurb: Not connected to the national park of the same name, Zion's Crag is a small bouldering spot in the Oquirrh Mountains on the west side of the Salt Lake Valley, in a dry ravine beside a Herriman neighborhood. The walls stand roughly 10 to 20 feet tall. All 17 problems are bouldering, spanning V0 up to V10, with the largest cluster around V6 and a good handful of harder lines above that. The rock has plenty of features, but holds can snap under load, so test each one before committing. A crash pad and a spotter are sensible here given the height.

ut_aguaworld.blurb: Aguaworld is a steep quartzite cliff near the mouth of Big Cottonwood Canyon in the Central Wasatch. Seventeen routes are on record: ten sport, six trad and one top rope. Grades start around 5.9 and reach into the low 5.12s, with most of the climbing at 5.10 and 5.11, so it suits climbers who are comfortable above the moderate range. Expect pumpy, sustained pulling on steep rock, and a few unbolted lines that feel serious. The wall catches plenty of sun, so cooler days or mornings are the better time to go, and despite the name there is no water at the base.

ut_baby_rubicon.blurb: Baby Rubicon is a small sport wall in Crawdad Canyon near Veyo, just downstream along the base from the bigger Rubicon wall. All 17 routes are bolted, and the grades cover a friendly range: a few very easy lines, a fair number of 5.7 to 5.9 climbs, and several at 5.10, with nothing harder than that. The wall is shaded for most of the day, which makes it a comfortable choice when the weather is warm, and a couple of routes have a tree handy for the belayer to lean against. Good for beginners stepping up and mid-grade climbers looking for a quick, relaxed session.

ut_sun_king_ruined_rock_wall.blurb: The Ruined Rock Wall is the west side of the Sun King, a rock dome in the Devil's Playground and Spires zone of Utah's West Desert, within the Aiguille du RV group of crags known for patina climbing. It holds 17 routes, 15 of them sport and two trad. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.11, with the heart of the wall at 5.9 and 5.10, so it works well for solid intermediate climbers. Because the dome has climbing on both its sides, you can usually find sun or shade for much of the day. A short uphill walk from the lower west camp reaches the base.

vt_nichols_ledge.blurb: Nichols Ledge is a granite cliff of about 200 feet in Woodbury, in north-central Vermont, reached from the Hardwick or Cabot side. It faces southwest, so it warms up and dries fast, which stretches the season well into autumn. The 17 routes split between sport (ten) and trad (seven), and the grades lean hard: one easy 5.7, a few 5.9 and 5.10 lines, then a big cluster at 5.11 and a handful of 5.12 and 5.13 pitches. The rock is steep and technical, with a mix of powerful moves and delicate smears. Poison ivy grows at the base. Expect good views and few other climbers.
